cognate: ON kné ~ Gk γόνυ (*ǵónu), the knees OF THE PERSON SUPPLICATED, as the place the suppliant goes or reaches to
drift_or_renewal: verb renewed: Gk 'take/touch the knees' (λαβέσθαι/ἅψασθαι γούνων), also 'come facing the knees' (ἀντίος ἤλυθε γούνων, Il. 20.463); ON 'go/stand before someone's knees' (ganga/fara fyrir kné e-m; here stondum firir yðrum kníom)
shared_syntax: verb of approach/contact + the addressee's knees (Gk genitive γούνων; ON fyrir + possessive + kné), the addressee being the one asked for mercy
context: Both slab passages are supplication for life or mercy: in Þiðreks saga the citizens lay down arms, open the town and come barefoot to 'stand before your knees' in surrender; in Herodotus the herdsman's wife takes her husband's knees, weeping, to beg him not to expose the child. Homer uses the same gesture for suppliants of Achilles and Zeus; Njáls saga uses the ON idiom without a foreign model, so it is not just a calque of the Low German source of Þiðreks saga
phrase: Gk γούνων λαβέσθαι / ἀντίος ἐλθεῖν γούνων ~ ON ganga fyrir kné e-m: approaching the knees of the supplicated
